book.deadrecall.remnant.manual.title: Remnant Survival Guide
book.deadrecall.remnant.basics.title: Backpacks and upgrades
book.deadrecall.remnant.basics.page.1:
Getting the guide

Use a guide or %1$s on a %2$s to record the Remnant method guide. A guide is kept; one %1$s becomes the new guide.

Right-click a backpack to open it, or press E to move items directly through its side-panel slots.
book.deadrecall.remnant.basics.page.2:
Smithing upgrades

All normal backpacks are made and upgraded at a Smithing Table. The three input slots shown at right are template, base, and addition.

Basic: 9 slots / 1 module
Standard: 18 / 2
Advanced: 27 / 3
Netherite: 36 / 4
book.deadrecall.remnant.dyeing.title: Backpack dyeing
book.deadrecall.remnant.dyeing.page.1:
Dyeing

Craft any normal backpack with one or more vanilla dyes. Re-dyeing mixes colors like leather armor and preserves contents and custom data.

Use a dyed backpack on a water-filled cauldron to wash it. %1$s cannot be dyed.
book.deadrecall.remnant.echo_crystalliza:
Echo crystallization

Use one %1$s on a %2$s block to crystallize its stored experience into one %3$s. The Sculk is exhausted into %4$s and releases no experience.

Sensors, Shriekers, Catalysts, and Sculk Veins cannot be crystallized.
book.deadrecall.remnant.module_recipes.o:
Reading each spread

The left page explains one module and its cautions. The right page displays the recipe currently enabled in this world.

If a data pack removes or disables that recipe, the right page marks it unavailable.
book.deadrecall.remnant.module_recipes.d:
%1$s

Enables an embedded 3x3 crafting grid in the backpack screen. Its output strictly follows this world's live data-pack recipes and cannot bypass a removed or changed recipe.

%1$s

Uses live 3x3 recipes to compact raw metals, iron/gold nuggets, and iron/copper/gold/netherite ingots. It safely chains tiers; incomplete leftovers are never consumed.

%1$s

On pickup, an item is routed into this backpack when it already contains the same kind. New item kinds remain in the player inventory.

%1$s

Each module adds one 9-slot row. The added slots are checked before removal; the module cannot be removed while any of them still contains an item.

%1$s

Consumed on player death to retain this backpack and its contents once instead of dropping it normally. Install another module after it is used.

%1$s

Combines blast and cactus protection in one upgrade slot. A dropped backpack cannot be destroyed by explosions or cactus damage.

%1$s

Protects a dropped normal backpack from fire, lava, and hot floors. Netherite Backpacks are intrinsically fireproof and do not need it.

%1$s

Prevents a dropped backpack from naturally despawning over time. The effect is permanent while installed and occupies one upgrade slot.

%1$s

Rescues a backpack that falls below the world and rejects direct void damage. It is not consumed; Netherite Backpacks do not include it.

%1$s

Adds an Ender button beside the backpack. The server opens only your own vanilla Ender Chest; no Ender items are copied into the backpack.
book.deadrecall.remnant.recipe.live: Shows the current world's live recipe
book.deadrecall.remnant.recipe.unavailab: This item cannot be crafted in this world
Dropped-item modules

%1$s combines both hazards in one slot. %2$s and %3$s each use one slot. %4$s protects %5$s, %6$s, and %7$s from fire, lava, and hot floors. %8$s is intrinsically fireproof.

%1$s

A normal backpack with this module is rescued below the world and rejects direct void damage. It is permanent but occupies one slot; %6$s does not include it.

See the Module recipe gallery for the complete ingredient layout.
book.deadrecall.remnant.death_backpack.p:
On death

When keepInventory is false, carried items are captured before normal drops into one red %1$s of up to 54 slots. Portable containers remain separate while nesting prevention is enabled.

The %1$s has a red locator beam.

Recovery

A %1$s does not despawn, resists ordinary damage, and is rescued below the void. By default, only its owner may open it. Empty every slot and close it to finish recovery.

Legacy ownerless packs remain recoverable. Curse of Vanishing still takes priority.
book.deadrecall.remnant.container_safety:
No unsafe nesting

While enabled by default, Remnant backpacks, %1$s, %2$s, and tagged portable containers cannot be placed inside one another. Existing nested contents are not deleted: remove them, but they cannot be inserted again.

World rule (default: true)

Allow Remnant nesting:
/gamerule totem:remnant_prevent_portable_container_nesting false

Disabling it removes only Remnant's added restrictions; vanilla restrictions remain.

Admins can run:
/deadrecall containers scan
